description: This pie chart, from the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the distribution of four distinct bias categories within a dataset, totaling 100% with a sample size of 100 (sum of the counts: 30 + 28 + 22 + 20). The chart is divided into four colored slices: the largest segment, “Right bias,” is dark blue and accounts for 30.0% (30); the second largest, “Left bias,” is orange and represents 28.0% (28); the third, “Left center bias,” is red and constitutes 20.0% (20); and the smallest, “Left center bias,” is green and makes up 22.0% (22). Each category is labeled with its name, percentage, and absolute count in parentheses. The chart includes a legend bar at the bottom left, though it is grayed out and does not provide additional color-key information. The slices are arranged in a clockwise descending order by size, starting from the top right with “Right bias.”
